group_pid_desc: PID (Proportional-Integral-Derivative) controller for precise wheel positioning and feedback response.
help_motion_range: Total rotation angle of the steering wheel (e.g., 900 degrees).
help_total_effect_strength: Global Strength: Defines the maximum output power of all effects.
help_static_dampening_strength: Static Dampening: Constant resistance to movement (Weight).
help_dynamic_dampening_strength: Dynamic Dampening (Friction): Resistance increases with speed.
help_integrated_spring_strength: Centering Spring: Returns the wheel to the center (for games without FFB).
help_power_limit: Maximum current/power allowed for the motor.
help_braking_limit: Maximum braking force (regenerative/resistive) of the motor.
help_pole_pairs: Number of magnetic pole pairs of the motor (See motor spec).
help_amplifier_gain: Sensitivity adjustment for the motor driver.
help_proportional_gain: Proportional (P): Defines how fast the motor reacts to position error.
help_integral_gain: Integral gain to limit steady-state error.
help_direct_x_constant_strength: Scales the strength of Constant effects from games.
help_direct_x_periodic_strength: Scales the strength of Periodic effects (Sine, Square, Triangle).
help_direct_x_spring_strength: Scales the strength of Spring effects requested by the game.
help_calibration_speed: Speed at which the wheel rotates during auto-calibration.
help_calibration_magnitude: Force applied during the calibration process.
help_encoder_direction: Inverts the motor encoder reading. Use if the position increases to the wrong side.
help_force_direction: Inverts the output force direction. Use if the wheel pushes away instead of centering.
help_debug_torque: Sends raw torque values to logs for debugging.
help_invert_game_force: Inverts the direction of Constant Force effects coming from the game.
msg_keyboard_warning: Note: Keyboard mapping requires the 'Mapping Service' to be running.
tool_ffb_desc: Live manual Force Feedback testing. Sliders reset to 0 when released.
help_edit_mapping: Configure button and keyboard mappings for this axis
help_axis_invert: Reverse the direction of the axis input
protocol_desc_none: No extension protocol active. The wheel operates in standalone mode without external peripherals.
protocol_desc_buttons: Extends the available buttons using GPIO pins. Adds up to 32 digital buttons through direct pin mapping.
protocol_desc_tm: Thrustmaster SPI protocol for connecting original TM shifters and button boxes. Uses SPI communication for fast, reliable button states.
protocol_desc_fanatec: Fanatec SPI protocol for connecting original Fanatec shifters and handbrakes. Compatible with CSL and ClubSport accessories.
protocol_compat_buttons: Any momentary switch or button connected directly to GPIO pins. Supports both common ground and common VCC configurations.
protocol_compat_tm: Thrustmaster TH8A shifter, sequential shifter, and official button boxes. Some third-party TM-compatible devices may also work.
protocol_compat_fanatec: Fanatec CSL shifter, ClubSport shifter, and handbrake. Requires proper connector wiring (check pinout diagram).
protocol_config_buttons: Configure pin modes in the Pins tab. Set each GPIO pin to 'Button' mode and assign button numbers in the Buttons tab.
protocol_config_tm: Set SPI pins (CS, SCK, MISO) in the Pins tab. No additional calibration needed - the protocol auto-detects button presses.
protocol_config_fanatec: Set SPI pins (CS, SCK, MISO) in the Pins tab. Ensure correct power supply (usually 5V). Check connector pinout before connecting.
protocol_tips_none: To add buttons or shifters, select an appropriate extension mode above.
protocol_tips_buttons: Use pull-up or pull-down resistors for clean signals. Test each button in the Monitor tab after configuration. Debouncing is handled in firmware.
protocol_tips_tm: If buttons don't respond, check SPI wiring (especially ground). Some shifters require 5V power. Monitor SPI communication in the Logs tab if issues persist.
protocol_tips_fanatec: Ensure CS (chip select) pin is correctly configured. Power supply voltage is critical - verify with multimeter. Check the official pinout diagram for your specific device.
